transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-07
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Marcus Allen (CTO - OpalPay), Lina Gomez (Head of ML), Devon Price (SRE), Sanjay Patel (Product)
Links referenced: security deck (https://redwood.app/security/opalpay), benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood.app/benchmarks/opalpay-48h)

[00:00] Jordan Reyes: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, I think we've got about an hour, appreciate you squeezing this in. quick intros?
[00:07] Marcus Allen: Marcus here, CTO, i'll keep it high level, thanks.
[00:10] Lina Gomez: Lina, head of ML, i'll talk traffic and prompts.
[00:13] Devon Price: Devon, SRE, I'll own infra questions.
[00:15] Sanjay Patel: Sanjay, product, here for success criteria.
[00:18] Jordan Reyes: great, from Redwood, Priya SE and I will run scoping. goal today: nail down workload characterization - QPS, concurrency, token distributions - so we can size a POC and run a meaningful 48-hour benchmark.
[00:30] Priya Singh: quick note, we'll propose both hosted and dedicated runs; dedicated gives predictable throughput, hosted is faster to start.
[00:36] Marcus Allen: our main constraints: latency under 300ms p95 on inference path for customer-facing flows, and cost per 1k requests needs to be below our internal target. also data residency, we need audit logs.
[00:48] Jordan Reyes: ok noted, latency p95 300ms, cost target — can you give a number for ops to compare?
[00:52] Sanjay Patel: we're aiming for < $0.20 per call (rough baseline) for the typical confirmation message generation.
[00:58] Priya Singh: helpful. for workload, Lina, can you walk through the types of prompts and tokens?
[01:03] Lina Gomez: sure, um, we have three main flows: 1) transaction summarization (short prompts, 20-60 input tokens, 30-80 output tokens), 2) multi-turn dispute resolution chat (longer context, avg 600 input tokens incl conversation history, outputs 80-300 tokens occasionally), 3) routing/classification for fraud triage (very short, 10-20 tokens in, 5-15 out).
[01:25] Lina Gomez: distribution roughly 60% summarization, 25% chat, 15% classification. token-wise median input length ~45, median output ~50 but there's a long tail for chat.
[01:36] Priya Singh: great — that's exactly what we need. traffic shape? QPS and concurrency?
[01:41] Marcus Allen: average QPS across the global app is about 25 QPS, peaks to ~220 QPS during promo windows. concurrency for models we think about in terms of in-flight tokens; at peak our chat flow has ~120 concurrent users, but because chat has longer outputs the token generation concurrency is higher.
[01:58] Devon Price: to add, our system does bursts — short spikes that last 5-15 minutes, then back to baseline. we can share a 24h log extract.
[02:05] Jordan Reyes: perfect — for sizing a POC we recommend modeling a typical steady-state at 30 QPS with burst tests up to 250 QPS, and set concurrency targets per model. we'll map those into GPU counts and batching config.
[02:18] Priya Singh: rough mapping: for the summarization model (short outputs), one rtx-class GPU with batching can handle ~200-400 tokens/sec depending on quantization; chat with 600+ token context depends a lot on kv-cache behavior. we usually test both low-latency config and cost-optimized config.
[02:35] Sanjay Patel: what's the expectation for latency under batching? our p95 300ms target is strict.
[02:40] Priya Singh: batching can increase throughput but may impact tail latency. Redwood offers dynamic batching with latency SLO knob; during the POC we'll run configurations: batch size caps and max wait times to hit p95 targets. for p95 300ms, we may need smaller batches or dedicated nodes.
[02:55] Marcus Allen: what about token distribution for billing? we need estimates to compare to our cost model.
[02:59] Jordan Reyes: we can use the token distributions Lina provided and run sample runs to estimate per-call token usage; we'll produce a cost projection for hosted vs dedicated.
[03:08] Priya Singh: also quantization—if you can tolerate minimal quality delta, int8/4-bit reduces memory and raises throughput which drops cost. we'll run quality regression on your eval set.
[03:20] Lina Gomez: quality delta must be <1% downstream metric impact, we have an eval set for transaction summarization and dispute resolution. we'll share that.
[03:27] Jordan Reyes: noted — success criteria: 1) p95 latency <= 300ms for customer flows, 2) per-call cost <= $0.20 (hosted) or better on dedicated, 3) negligible quality regression on your eval set, 4) security: SOC2 + KMS for keys and audit logs enabled. are we aligned?
[03:46] Sanjay Patel: yes, aligned.
[03:48] Devon Price: for POC infra we want a private VPC option so traffic doesn't traverse public internet, and customer-managed KMS is required for keys.
[03:58] Priya Singh: Redwood Private supports VPC/on-prem and KMS/HSM; for POC we can run in a private VPC in our cloud region or spin up Dedicated nodes in your VPC if needed. we'll include config notes.
[04:10] Marcus Allen: good. what does the 48-hour benchmark look like operationally?
[04:14] Jordan Reyes: we propose: 48-hour run with real-ish traffic replayed (you provide 24h logs, we replay baseline + bursts), measure p50/p95/p99 token latencies, throughput, GPU utilization, and error rates. also run quality evals pre/post to detect regressions. we'll provide a reproducible benchmark repo and scripts.
[04:31] Priya Singh: timeline: if you give logs and token distributions this week, SE can configure benchmark by Apr 12, run 48-hour test Apr 14-16, and debrief Apr 18.
[04:40] Lina Gomez: that timeline works for us, we'll get logs and eval set by Apr 9.
[04:44] Jordan Reyes: perfect. question: do you have internal rules around throughput limiting or rate limiting? will we be able to push bursts for the benchmark?
[04:50] Devon Price: we can open a bench subnet, but need safe caps — we'll allow push to 300 QPS for 15-minute windows.
[04:57] Priya Singh: good, that fits the plan. for modeling concurrency, we'll need to estimate average generation length per call — Lina said median 50 output tokens but chat can be up to 300. please confirm distribution tail numbers in the spreadsheet.
[05:10] Lina Gomez: will do, I'll populate the benchmark sheet with percentiles: p50 input 45 tokens, p95 input 620 tokens, output p50 48, p95 280.
[05:22] Jordan Reyes: thanks. any compliance questions now?
[05:25] Marcus Allen: SOC2 is required, plus retention rules — we keep logs for 7 years for audit, and PII must be redacted before storing. can Redwood provide audit log exports?
[05:35] Priya Singh: yes, we provide audit logs and can integrate with your SIEM. retention policy configurable; we can also enable redaction hooks. we'll add specifics in the security deck.
[05:45] Sanjay Patel: for fallback behaviour during capacity issues — what are options?
[05:49] Jordan Reyes: smart routing and fallbacks: we can route to smaller lower-cost model variants, or to a cached response for frequent prompts. also circuit-breakers and graceful degradation are configurable. we'll include recommended policies for test.
[06:00] Devon Price: for the POC we want to validate fallback end-to-end. include synthetic tests that trigger capacity constraints.
[06:06] Priya Singh: yes we'll design a canary + failover test.
[06:09] Jordan Reyes: ok to recap and confirm action items?
[06:11] Marcus Allen: sure.
[06:12] Jordan Reyes: recap: OpalPay will share 24h traffic logs, percentile token distributions, and eval datasets by Apr 9. Redwood (Priya) will prepare benchmark config and run 48-hour tests Apr 14-16. Jordan will share pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated and the security deck by Apr 9. Post-run debrief Apr 18. action items in workspace.
[06:33] Sanjay Patel: one last Q, do you have examples of similar customers and their throughput numbers?
[06:37] Priya Singh: yes we have benchmark case studies (we mentioned banks and payments customers) — we'll share anonymized numbers and typical GPU counts and cost ranges.
[06:45] Marcus Allen: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:47] Jordan Reyes: thanks, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and kickoff the config.
[06:50] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional words mis-transcribed: "kv cache" appears as "k v cash" in one excerpt; proper nouns occasionally inconsistent (OpalPay typed as OpalPay or Opal Pay in auto transcript). There is some crosstalk at 03:20-03:30.
